clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Sabrina presented with a cheerful and cooperative demeanor, though her attention span was notably inconsistent, leading to fluctuations in task engagement. Her muscle tone was within normal limits, with full range of motion observed across major joints. Despite a generally positive affect, Sabrina displayed significant distractibility, necessitating frequent verbal cues and redirection to sustain focus during activities. She exhibited stronger engagement in structured tasks compared to self-directed activities, although she needed maximal visual cues to complete more complex directives. Fine motor coordination was suboptimal, particularly noted during visual-motor integration tasks where hand-over-hand assistance was occasionally required. The aforementioned factors influenced the validity of standardized testing scores, prompting necessary adaptations to procedures and reinforcing the need for a supportive testing environment.
